note: Q.7 a.1 co. says of God that his esse 'non sit esse receptum in aliquo, sed ipse sit suum esse subsistens', and ad 3 that his esse is 'per se subsistens non receptum in aliquo', as a whiteness 'non esset in alio' would be subsistent whiteness. The passage asserts both of God and pairs them in the example; it does not state the general conditional that whatever has unreceived esse is its own being. The existing claim reads the sentence through a represented essence/esse equality, not through own being.
